differences: The paper reports 504 participants and 5,544 steps recorded originally (Introduction, Methods); the deposit holds the 469 participants and 5,159 steps of the analysis set (Table 3), so the 35 left out (2 with missing data, 33 of the youngest controls removed for age matching) are not here.

Table 3's age at diagnosis (Parkinson's disease 58.26, differential diagnoses 52.96, multiple sclerosis 43.82, other 55.02 years) is reproduced only when the deposit's 0 (unknown, 19 participants) is replaced by the participant's age, which the paper does not state; dropping the zeros instead gives 58.08, 52.23, 40.67 and 54.14. The deposit itself repeats the age for all healthy controls, for whom Table 3 shows no value. participants.csv leaves both empty.

The paper and the PhysioNet page name the Apple Watch Series 4 only; the deposit's observation files list the Series 3 for 135 of the 469 participants, and device and watch_model follow the observation files.
The PhysioNet description says each file holds 1024 samples (10.24 s); the three 20-s steps (1a, 1b, 10) have 2048 samples per file, as the paper's Table 4 durations imply.
The deposit gives one participant a height of 55 cm (an entry error); it is kept as shared, and Table 3's healthy-control height SD (15.63) is reproduced only with it.
